source.title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory

accepted.question_text: Construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories that satisfy the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal, and Moore-Seiberg, or at least prove that such rational conformal field theories exist. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and the minimal models, or prove their existence as rational conformal field theories satisfying those axioms.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Construct rational conformal ﬁeld theories satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal [Se] and Moore-Seiberg [MS1] [ MS2], or at least prove the existence of such rational conformal ﬁeld theories. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and minimal models or at least prove their existence.

accepted.question_text: Prove that the series formed from intertwining operators and used to build higher-genus correlation functions actually converge, so that these series can define higher-genus correlation functions in rational conformal field theory.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Prove the convergence of these series obtained using intertwining operators to construct higher-genus correlation functions.

accepted.question_text: Suppose the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has an inner product that is invariant under the conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators. Is the locally convex topological completion obtained by adjoining elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces isomorphic, as a locally convex topological vector space with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form, to the Hilbert-space completion of that graded state space?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3. If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal ﬁeld theory has a compatible inner product, then the locally convex topological comple- tion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces and the Hilbert space completion are isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces with grading structures and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian forms.

accepted.question_text: For a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length completely reducible if and only if, for every positive integer n, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule vanishes? Equivalently, for a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is complete reducibility of every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length equivalent to vanishing of the n-th cohomology for every positive integer n and every bimodule?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. Every grading-restricted generalized module of ﬁnite length for a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if forn∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coeﬃcients in any bimodule is 0. In particular, every grading-restricted generalized module of ﬁnite length for a grading-restricted vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n ∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coeﬃcients in any bimodule (whose left and right actions can be diﬀerent) is 0.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra associated to a Wess-Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra, or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra. Is it true that, for every positive integer n, the n-th cohomology of V, viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any V-bimodule, is zero?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra associated to a Wess- Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra. Then forn∈ Z+, then-th cohomology of V as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coeﬃcients in any V -bimodule is 0.

accepted.question_text: Find a criterion stated purely in terms of a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself that guarantees complete reducibility of its modules.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Find a criterion on a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself for the complete reducibility of modules.

accepted.question_text: Study the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories by giving it topological and geometric structures, and prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in that moduli space.
accepted.context_brief: Moduli space of conformal field theories

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Study the moduli space of conformal ﬁeld theories. Give topo- logical and geometric structures on the moduli space. Prove that rational conformal ﬁeld theories are isolated points in the moduli space.

accepted.question_text: Determine conditions under which formal deformations of grading-restricted vertex algebras converge to analytic deformations, and generalize the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Find the conditions for the formal deformations of grading- restricted vertex algebras to converge to analytic deformations. Generalize the de- formation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal ﬁeld theories.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra such that V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, and V is C2-cofinite. Is the braided tensor category constructed in the cited work [H8] from [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] rigid?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n< 0 and the contragredient V′, as a V -module, is equivalent to V .

(2) V is C2-coﬁnite, that is, dimV/C 2(V )<∞, where C2(V ) is the subspace of V spanned by the elements of the form Resxx−2Y (u,x )v for u,v ∈ V and Y :V⊗V →V [[x,x−1]] is the vertex operator map for V . Then the braided tensor category given in [H8] based on the work [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] is rigid.

accepted.question_text: Give a definition of modular tensor category appropriate for the nonsemisimple setting, prove that the braided tensor category from Conjecture 5.1 has such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category structure, and determine whether such a category still yields a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Give a deﬁnition of modular tensor category in the nonsemisim- ple case and prove that the braided tensor category in Conjecture 5.1 has such a modular tensor category structure. From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor cat- egory, can we still construct a 3-dimensional topological quantum ﬁeld theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the hypotheses of Conjecture 5.1, namely that V is simple, V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, and V is C2-cofinite. Can one construct genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions from the corresponding genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions, and from those full correlation functions construct a conformal field theory satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich-Segal except for the axioms involving unitarity?
accepted.context_brief: Full correlation functions in logarithmic CFT

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n< 0 and the contragredient V′, as a V -module, is equivalent to V .

Problem 5.3. For a vertex operator algebra satisfying the conditions in Con- jecture 5.1, is it possible to construct genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions from the genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions? From these genus-zero and genus-one correlation functions, is it possible to construct a conformal ﬁeld theory satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich-Segal, except for the axioms involving unitarity?

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra such that V satisfies the two conditions from Conjecture 5.1, namely V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, and V is C2-cofinite, and assume in addition that every grading-restricted generalized V-module is completely reducible. For a finite group G of automorphisms of V, do the twisted intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?
accepted.context_brief: Twisted intertwining operators for finite orbifolds

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n< 0 and the contragredient V′, as a V -module, is equivalent to V .

Conjecture 6.1. LetV be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two condi- tions in Conjecture 5.1. Assume that in addition every grading-restricted general- izedV -module is completely reducible. Let G be a ﬁnite group of automorphisms of V . Then the twisted intertwining operators among the g-twistedV -modules for all g∈G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the three conditions used in Conjecture 6.1: V satisfies V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, V is C2-cofinite, and every grading-restricted generalized V-module is completely reducible. Let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Is the category of g-twisted V-modules for all g in G a G-crossed tensor category in the sense of Turaev?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.2. LetV be a vertex operator satisfying the three conditions in Conjecture 6.1 and let G be a ﬁnite group of automorphisms of V . The the category of g-twisted V -modules for all g∈G is a G-crossed (tensor) category in the sense of Turaev [T2].

For a finite group G of automorphisms of V, do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?

Then the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among theg-twistedV -modules for all g∈G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

(2) V is C2-coﬁnite, that is, dimV/C 2(V )<∞, where C2(V ) is the subspace of V spanned by the elements of the form Resxx−2Y (u,x )v for u,v ∈ V and Y :V⊗V →V [[x,x−1]] is the vertex operator map for V . accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra and G a group of automorphisms of V. When G is infinite, under what conditions do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance, and under what conditions is the category of all g-twisted V-modules a G-crossed tensor category?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Let V be a vertex operator algebra and let G be a group of automorphisms of V . If G is an inﬁnite group, under what conditions do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V -modules for all g∈ G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties? Under what conditions is the category of g-twisted V -modules for all g∈ G a G-crossed (tensor) category?

accepted.question_text: Suppose V is a vertex operator algebra whose central charge is 24, whose weight-1 subspace is zero, and whose irreducible V-modules are all equivalent to V while every V-module is completely reducible. Must V be isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The central charge of V is 24.

(2) V has no nonzero elements of weight 1. (3) Any irreducible V module is equivalent to V as a V -module and every V -module is completely reducible. Then V must be isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra.

accepted.question_text: Suppose V is a vertex operator algebra whose central charge is 24 and such that every irreducible V-module is equivalent to V while every V-module is completely reducible. Is V uniquely determined by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the ﬁrst and the third conditions in Conjecture 7.1. Then V is determined uniquely by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight 1.
Conjecture 7.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The central charge of V is 24.
(3) Any irreducible V module is equivalent to V as a V -module and every V -module is completely reducible.

accepted.question_text: Construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold corresponds to the N = 2 vertex operator superalgebra of the Gepner model and such that deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N = 2 superconformal field theories.
accepted.context_brief: Calabi-Yau to N=2 vertex operator superalgebras

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quin- tic threefold corresponds to the N = 2 vertex operator superalgebra for the Gepner model and such that deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deforma- tions of N = 2 superconformal ﬁeld theories.

accepted.question_text: If one can construct N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds, then study their representation theory and use it to construct the corresponding N = 2 superconformal field theories, including proofs of the operator product expansion of intertwining operators and of modular invariance, together with the construction of modular tensor categories in a suitable sense and of full N = 2 superconformal field theories.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. IfN = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi- Yau manifolds can be constructed, study the representation theory of these N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras. Use this representation theory to construct the cor- respondingN = 2 superconformal ﬁeld theories, including the proof of the operator product expansion of intertwining operators, the proof of modular invariance, the construction of modular tensor categories (in a suitable sense), and the construction of full N = 2 superconformal ﬁeld theories.

accepted.question_text: Assume that N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds have been constructed, that the basic representation-theoretic results for those algebras have been obtained, and that the full N = 2 superconformal field theories have been constructed. Under those assumptions, formulate and prove physicists’ conjectures on Calabi-Yau manifolds, such as quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry, by turning physicists’ intuition into mathematical methods using those results and constructions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3. Suppose thatN = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manidfolds can be constructed, that the basic results in the representa- tion theory of these algebras can be obtained and that the full N = 2 superconformal ﬁeld theories can be constructed. Formulate and prove the conjectures (for example, quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry) by physicists on Calabi-Yau manifolds by turning physicists’ intuition into mathematical methods using these results and constructions.

accepted.question_text: Find a direct connection between the representation-theoretic approach via vertex operator algebras and the approach via conformal nets, and prove that at least for rational conformal field theories these two approaches are equivalent.
accepted.context_brief: Vertex operator algebras and conformal nets

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1. Find a direct connection between the method of the represen- tation theory of vertex operator algebras and the method of conformal nets. Prove that at least for rational conformal ﬁeld theories, they are equivalent.
